extra.message: The /ops/bundle/dispatch-thaw-172 endpoint calls pickle.loads() on raw bytes taken directly from the request body or the 'blob' query parameter (optionally base64-decoded). Pickle deserialization of untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution via crafted __reduce__ payloads.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: The /ops/jinja/dispatch-cast-380 endpoint builds a Jinja2 template string by concatenating user-controlled 'fragment' query parameter directly into the template source ('Result: ' + fragment) before calling Template(...).render(). This is server-side template injection and can lead to remote code execution via Jinja2 sandbox-escape payloads (e.g. {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[...].__subclasses__() }}).

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: The /ops/xml/dispatch-fold-450 endpoint parses the raw request body with lxml.etree using an XMLParser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. This enables XML External Entity (XXE) processing, allowing an attacker-supplied XML document to read local files or trigger SSRF via external entity references.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The /ops/mongo/dispatch-lane-415 endpoint takes the 'filter' key of the JSON body (or the whole payload) and passes it unmodified as the MongoDB query document to find_one(). An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators (e.g. $where, $regex, $ne) to bypass intended filtering or execute expensive/arbitrary queries.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The /ops/formula/dispatch-cast-254 endpoint calls eval() on the user-supplied 'expr' query parameter. Although __builtins__ is restricted to an empty dict, eval() of attacker-controlled expressions is inherently unsafe — sandbox escapes via object introspection (e.g. accessing __class__.__base__.__subclasses__()) can still lead to arbitrary code execution.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: The /ops/badge/dispatch-gate-435 endpoint grants an elevated 'lane': 'elevated' response (exposing payroll/casework data) based solely on a client-supplied cookie or 'x-ops-badge' header equal to the static string 'lead', with no cryptographic verification, session check, or user authentication. Any caller who guesses or observes this value can impersonate an elevated/authorized identity.

cwe: CWE-287: Improper Authentication
CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The /ops/dock/dispatch-shelf-393 endpoint builds a file path as BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name using the client-controlled 'name' query parameter without sanitizing path separators or '..' sequences, then writes the request body to that path. An attacker can supply a name like '../../etc/cron.d/x' to write arbitrary files outside the intended export directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The /ops/vault/dispatch-stash-231 endpoint builds a target file path from the client-controlled 'ref' query/body parameter (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json') with no sanitization, allowing path traversal (e.g. ref='../../etc/x') to write files outside the export directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The /ops/vault/dispatch-stash-231 endpoint writes a raw SSN and full credit card number, taken directly from the request payload, to a plaintext JSON file on disk with no encryption. Sensitive financial/PII data at rest should never be stored unencrypted.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The /ops/blurb/dispatch-tile-320 endpoint renders the user-controlled 'card' query parameter through a Jinja2 template using the |safe filter, which disables Jinja2's autoescaping, and returns the result as an HTMLResponse. This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript that executes in the victim's browser (reflected XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The /ops/origin/dispatch-mirror-375 endpoint reflects the client-supplied Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This combination allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the response, defeating the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-346: Origin Validation Error
CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The /ops/after/dispatch-afterlane-021 endpoint redirects to the user-controlled 'lane' query parameter with no validation that it is a relative path or an allow-listed host, enabling an open redirect to attacker-controlled sites (e.g. lane=https://evil.example).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The /ops/spool/dispatch-fan-304 endpoint accepts a client-controlled 'count' integer with no upper bound and builds a list of that many rows in memory, allowing an attacker to trigger excessive memory/CPU consumption with a very large count value.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: The /ops/wire/dispatch-manifest-tally-020 endpoint logs the full raw request body and the Authorization header value at WARNING level. Logging credentials/auth material and unsanitized request content exposes sensitive data to anyone with log access and permits log injection via CR/LF in the body.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: The /ops/frame/dispatch-slip-425 endpoint explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and empties the Content-Security-Policy header, weakening browser-side XSS mitigations for this response.

cwe: CWE-16: Configuration

extra.message: The /ops/pulse/dispatch-csv-glitch-019 endpoint returns the raw exception message (including the internal BASE_EXPORT_DIR path and user-supplied lot_ref) and the exception class name directly in the JSON response, leaking internal implementation details to callers.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The /ops/trace/dispatch-panel-445 endpoint returns the raw APP_ENV environment variable value and the internal export base path in its JSON response, disclosing internal configuration details.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The /ops/identity/dispatch-hint-365 endpoint checks a client-supplied 'verifier' value against a hardcoded in-source dictionary of secrets ({'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}) using a plain '!=' comparison (not constant-time), acting as a weak, guessable, hardcoded authentication mechanism.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The internal ops gate compares the X-Internal-Token header to the INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN secret using a plain '!=' string comparison instead of a constant-time comparison (e.g. hmac.compare_digest). Since this token gates access to highly dangerous operations (pickle deserialization, eval, XXE, SSTI, etc.), a timing side-channel could aid brute-forcing the token.

cwe: CWE-208: Observable Timing Discrepancy

extra.message: In enqueue_event, _is_safe_url() validates the destination host/IP is not private/loopback/reserved before calling urllib.request.urlopen(), but urlopen follows HTTP redirects by default (noted in the code comment itself). A malicious or compromised webhook target URL can respond with a redirect to an internal address (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ or http://localhost/), bypassing the SSRF guard entirely once DISPATCH_WEBHOOKS_LIVE=1 is enabled.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: test_webhook() has the same SSRF weakness as enqueue_event: _is_safe_url() checks the target host once, but urllib.request.urlopen() follows redirects by default, allowing an admin-triggered 'test' request to a validated-looking URL to be redirected to an internal/private address and bypass the SSRF allow-list check.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: request_password_reset() writes the raw, unhashed password-reset token together with the user's email in plaintext to a persistent log file (password_reset_tokens.log) on every request. Anyone with read access to this file (or a log-aggregation pipeline that ingests it) can take over any account by using the token before it expires.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Settings.secret_key has a hardcoded fallback value ('dev-secret-do-not-use-in-production-this-is-long-enough') that is used to HMAC-sign every session token and API key hash if the SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. If this default ships to a production deployment, an attacker who knows this well-known string can forge/verify session and API-key hashes.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
CWE-259: Use of Hard-coded Password
